(Iryna Rybakova/Ukraine's 93rd Mechanized Brigade via AP) KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russian ballistic missiles struck the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv early on Sunday, setting off fires and wounding at least three civilians, while attacks on other parts of the country later killed at least two people, local officials said. The strikes came as Ukraine’s successful drone attacks have stalled the Russian army’s advances in an expanded campaign inside Russia that has been causing fuel shortages and piling pressure on Russian leader Vladimir Putin. In Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine, Kremlin-installed authorities said a Ukrainian drone strike had killed four civilians in the city of Horlivka. According to Ivan Prikhodko, the city’s Russian-appointed mayor, the city had been under fire since the early hours of Sunday. According to Russia’s defense ministry, Russian forces overnight struck down 133 Ukrainian drones over Russia, the Black Sea and Crimea, the peninsula that Moscow forcibly annexed from Ukraine in 2014. Russian attacks set fire to tower block near Kyiv’s center Blasts rocked Kyiv in the early hours of Sunday, with falling debris sparking a blaze in a tower block near the historic center, according to mayor Vitali Klitschko. Elsewhere in the city, falling debris set fire to buildings, cars and car parks, Klitschko added. He said three people had been wounded, with one needing hospital treatment. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned in his evening address on Friday that intelligence assessments indicated that Russia was preparing missiles for a large attack, saying there were indications that this could happen in the next 48 hours. Russia’s defense ministry claimed on Sunday that its latest attack on Kyiv had struck sites linked to drone production. Also Sunday, a drone strike on Kharkiv — Ukraine’s second-largest city in the east — killed one person and wounded at least six others, including two children, mayor Igor Terekhov reported. In the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, a Russian glide bomb killed one man and wounded at least six other people, according to mayor Ivan Fedorov. Both Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia have been frequent targets for Russian attacks, with Zaporizhzhia — just over 20 kilometers (12.5 miles) from the front line — suffering heavy bombardment in recent months. The war sees an escalation in tit-for-tat strikes On Friday, a major Russian strike near Kyiv killed at least 10 people and wounded around 100 others, part of a cycle of tit-for-tat attacks that dims the potential of reaching a diplomatic end to Russia’s more than 4-year-old invasion of its neighbor. Meanwhile, Finnish President Alexander Stubb claimed on Sunday that “Ukraine’s position is stronger than ever since the war began”. Following a call with his Ukrainian counterpart — and appearing to allude to Kyiv’s recent drone campaign that has struck major Russian energy sites and sought to choke off military supplies — Stubb wrote on X that “continued support from (Ukraine’s) partners is critical to keep up the momentum.” Putin calls on Russia’s navy to defend ‘shadow fleet’ tankers Putin said Western attempts to seize Russia-linked oil tankers amounted to “piracy,” and called on the Russian Navy to fight them. “We must act carefully in line with international maritime law but decisively — just as we must fight piracy and pirates,” Putin said Sunday during a speech marking Russia’s annual Navy Day. Moscow is believed to be using a fleet of hundreds of ships, many of them sailing under third-country flags, to ship oil in violation of international sanctions that followed its war on Ukraine. Last month, armed British forces boarded and detained a sanctioned tanker suspected of being part of this so-called “shadow fleet.” French authorities have also intercepted some of these vessels. Russia has traditionally marked Navy Day with a major naval parade in and near the city of St. Petersburg, with Putin personally reviewing warships. This year was the second time in a row the parade had been called off entirely while in 2024, it was scaled down. A British intelligence update published earlier this month linked the cancellations to “force protection” concerns, citing a successful Ukrainian attack on Jun. 3 against a Russian warship docked near St. Petersburg. Romania shoots down another suspected Russian drone Romania intercepted a suspected Russian drone in its airspace on Sunday, Romanian President Nicușor Dan said — the third such incursion in three days above the Eastern European nation that borders Ukraine and is a member of both NATO and the European Union. Dan called the incidents “inadmissible and intolerable” in a post on X and added that authorities found one of the earlier downed drones appears to be “a Shahed type, used by the Russian Federation in the war of aggression against Ukraine.” NATO said two Romanian F-16 fighter jets scrambled from Fetești airbase, under NATO’s operational command, in the morning hours and downed the drone over the Black Sea. A series of drone incursions by Russia and Ukraine have hit Romania and other NATO members since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/health/ambu.text: The Budapest Times Ambulance response times go public — and the numbers aren’t pretty Starting from Tuesday, the National Ambulance Service will make its response times public, the Minister of Health announced at a press conference in Budapest. Zsolt Hegedűs described the publication of the ambulance service’s response time data as a super-milestone. He said that a shift in approach is needed — one that is not afraid of transparency. “We must confront our own results” in order for emergency care to improve, he said. Miklós Constantinovits, acting director general of the OMSZ, said that in order to meet the targets — a 15-minute response time — the current situation must be faced head-on. In addition to response times, professional and operational indicators must also be measured, because without knowledge of these, the points for intervention will not be identified. He stressed that public education also needs to be strengthened. The website will be accessible from Tuesday at noon at stat.mentok.hu. The data will be updated monthly. The platform will present response times broken down at national, Budapest, and regional levels, separated by emergency category, as well as the number of rescue incidents. The website also helps users interpret the data: it explains, among other things, the meaning of average, median, and percentile, the process of calling an ambulance, and how and on what basis patients are classified by urgency. The director general emphasised that response time alone does not describe how the ambulance system operates, as it depends on factors including the road accessibility of a given incident location and whether there is an ambulance station nearby. According to data presented in advance to journalists, in July the arrival time in 90 percent of the most urgent cases (P1 category) — measured from the moment the emergency call was initiated — was 26.4 minutes nationally (12,123 cases), and 24.7 minutes in Budapest (2,408 cases). When asked about the ambulance service’s budget for next year, the health minister replied that planning for next year’s budget is currently underway, but disclosed that this year 36 new ambulances will be procured, and next year 200 vehicles are planned. He also announced that the application period for the position of director-general of the ambulance service has closed, and that from next week a five-member committee will interview the candidates, after which this body will submit its personnel recommendation to the minister. Photograph: Rocco Fazzari/AAP Sydney Beau Lamarre-Condon trial shown CCTV of accused’s movements across Sydney after alleged double murder Former NSW police officer has pleaded not guilty to February 2024 murders of Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29 Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Mon 5 Oct 2026 22.39 EDT Last modified on Mon 5 Oct 2026 22.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jurors have seen how dozens of CCTV cameras tracked Beau Lamarre-Condon’s movements across Sydney well into the night after he allegedly murdered his former partner. The 31-year-old former senior constable has pleaded not guilty to the murders of Jesse Baird and the 26-year-old’s new partner, Luke Davies, saying they were killed in two separate violent struggles. CCTV played for the NSW supreme court jury on Tuesday shows Lamarre-Condon arriving on foot at an Avis car rental depot at about 9pm on 19 February 2024, about 12 hours after the killings. ‘Don’t freak out’: Beau Lamarre-Condon asked friend if hire cars could be tracked before alleged murders, court hears Read more A receipt from his Uber account shows Lamarre-Condon hired a rideshare from Kensington, where he left his personal vehicle, to the rental car depot, prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC said. The accused can be seen driving out of the depot in a Toyota HiAce van, which was later discovered to have significant blood staining by forensics officers. GPS data from the van shows it was parked near the rear roller door of Baird’s house in Paddington at about 11pm, Hatfield said. It left 22 minutes later, he said. Further footage of the van near Baird’s house after midnight on February 20 would be played later in the trial, the prosecutor said. View image in fullscreen Luke Davies (left) and Jesse Baird (right), were allegedly murdered in Baird’s Paddington share house. Composite: Supplied/NSW Supreme Court The various vehicles Lamarre-Condon used to get around Sydney and its surrounds while cleaning up the alleged crime scene and disposing of two bodies have been a key part of the prosecution case. CCTV from another car hire business on February 18 – the day before the alleged murders – shows the former police officer’s mother hiring an SUV while her son waits outside. Lamarre-Condon got his mother to hire the Mazda CX-5 because he intended to only kill Baird, Hatfield previously told the jury. But after being surprised by Davies making a triple-zero call, he shot the 29-year-old through a door and had to upsize his vehicle and make extra purchases to accommodate the extra body, the prosecution has alleged. Audio of the triple-zero call made from Davies’ phone was played to the jury on Friday . After muffled words and sounds, an operator can be heard saying, “Caller disconnected, no request”. “I heard a male say, ‘eff off’, call dropped out,” she says. Lamarre-Condon’s barrister said his client made the call after killing Baird in self-defence but it was cut short by a second struggle in which Davies died. The men’s bodies were left in surfboard bags in the share house’s courtyard overnight. Baird’s housemates took a photo of red liquid leaking from the bag when they discovered it later that day. The purchase of the second surfboard bag after the deaths was a further indicator of the former officer adapting to the unexpected killing of Davies, the prosecution alleged. But Lamarre-Condon’s barrister says the lengths he went to in cleaning and disposing of the bodies showed his panic, rather than a murderous intent. The trial continues.
